fieldMarks: Medium-sized rail, 21-25 cm, with a long bill.
Rich rusty-cinnamon underparts contrasting with grey cheeks.
Sharp black-and-white bars on the flanks and reddish wings.
behavior: Seldom seen but often heard: a far-carrying 'ticket, ticket, ticket' and various grunts.
Probes mud and shallow water or stalks small prey; eats mostly aquatic insects and larvae, plus crayfish, snails and worms.
Most migrate to the southern United States and northern Mexico; some western U.S. populations may be resident.
habitat: Fresh and brackish marshes for nesting, often in drier spots than the sora where both breed; moves into salt marshes in winter.
range: Breeds across southern Canada and much of the United States and winters in the southern United States and northern Mexico, some as far as Guatemala.

lookalikes.name: King rail
lookalikes.howToTell: The king rail is much larger with tan or brownish rather than grey cheeks.

lookalikes.name: Sora
lookalikes.howToTell: The sora is short-billed with a yellow bill and black face; the Virginia rail is long-billed with grey cheeks.
